text: This Alpha Lab strategy beat buy & hold $BTC since we put it live in July. It bought before the August move, then went risk-off before the drop: up 19% vs. 6% for holding. Alpha Lab is our proprietary backtesting engine. Try it out 👈

Bitcoin's newest buyers are responsible for the current sell pressure. Coins bought in the last six months now change hands at a loss, after 2 rounds of profit taking since August. The question now is whether they panic underneath the current cost basis cluster.

In our new research, we introduce Book Churn, a metric that counts how often the order book is rewritten. We look at what depth and spread miss, and test churn as a volatility signal on BTC and ETH perpetuals. Full research article 👈

Bitcoin miners are rapidly selling their reserves. For years, listed miners held what they mined, and some bought more. Since January, they have sold nearly half their $BTC. A major shift in their approach: the BTC now funds their move into AI data centers.

Bids have stacked up below $BTC for weeks, yet price kept falling regardless. Takers sold into a bid-heavy book, continually grinding price downward. As soon as this sell-side aggression flips, we expect this imbalance to favor a sharp bounce.

Thick short term holder support is likely to provide some relief for $BTC here. These levels tend to act as support as long as price remains above them. If broken, we expect short term holders to capitulate, forcing price down further.

$BTC trades near $64k on Monday after a weekly slide of about 13%. Leverage was flushed and ETF selling continued, while short-term holders sit at a loss and loss-taking is the heaviest since July. Read our latest BTC Market Pulse 👈

Short-term holder supply in profit is dropping rapidly. In a range-bound environment, this metric is particularly useful for estimating tops and bottoms. It flashed bright red after $BTC's August spike and remained elevated until the recent washout accelerated.
